chapter: Rose Murphy, wartime 52nd Street, Town Hall
title: The 1945 Town Hall concert and the Indiana duet with Don Byas
summary: At Town Hall promoter Timmie Rosenkrantz asked Stewart and Don Byas to open the second half as a duo with no rhythm section; they played about twelve choruses of Indiana.

blocks.x: Now, about 1945, you played at this concert in Town Hall.
At Town Hall, yes, right.
You recorded with --

Well, there was a group of musicians. Let's see, most prominent in my mind is the tenor alto -- no, tenor sax man, Don Byas. He was on the bill with us and I think Lee Young from the Coast was playing drums on this particular engagement. I'm not sure.
Do you remember what different bands?
Well, there was a mixed-up band there. They had quite a group. I can't recall. But I do remember Don Byas.
(Laughter.)
How was the -- how did it come about that the two of you ended up doing the duets on "Indiana" and "I Got Rhythm."

That's right. Now, during the show -- or during intermission Timmie Rosenkrantz, who was running the show, came up to Don and myself and said to us, "Hey, Slam and Don, why don't the two of you, when we go back on stage, just the two of you, why don't you do something

between the two of you?" I don't know whether he was trying to put us on or what have you, but he mentioned "Why don't the two of you go out there and do a couple of numbers for us, to start the show off, you know."
To start the second half?

Yeah, the second half, sure. And I started wondering, what in the world could just two of us, no rhythm, no piano, no nothing to accompany us and what have you, and Don -- I talked with Don about it and he said, "Oh, man, I think we can do that," you know. "You just go ahead and stomp off -- name a couple of tunes and you stomp it off in a certain tempo and I'll take it from there and I'll take two or three choruses and then you come on in and play a couple of choruses or so and we'll just take it on from there, you know, and ad lib it on out," you know. So that's what we did.
How did the audience respond?
Oh, my goodness. We started off with -- what was that number?
"Indiana."

"Indiana?" And my goodness. Of course, while we were playing, you could -- naturally, you could hear a pin drop- I might add this, our rhythm section was myself and my size-12 shoe pounding on the floor.
(Laughter.)
And every once in a while, you could hear my foot
really pounding on that stage floor there. But somehow, Don and I, we just played and played. On "Indiana," I think we played about maybe between us about 12 or more choruses, you know?
Uh-huh.
